title: How the ZPA Terraform provider resolves the enrollment certificate for connector, service edge and private cloud groups

prose.text: App Connector, Service Edge and Private Cloud groups share one enrollment-certificate resolver. {{cert-optional-computed}}
The same fix as seen from the product: [[zpa.app-connectors.connector-groups]] and [[zpa.private-service-edges.enrollment]]. User code verification is separate: [[zpa.terraform.resource-fidelity]].

read-hydrates-write-sends-state.statement: Read copies enrollment_cert_id from the API response into state, and the request expander sends whatever value the resource data currently holds.

quotes: _ = d.Set("enrollment_cert_id", resp.EnrollmentCertID)

empty-string-selects-lookup.statement: An explicit empty string for enrollment_cert_id does not clear the certificate. The resolver looks the certificate up by name only when the resource data holds no nonempty value, which is on create or on an update of a group whose state is also empty; on other updates the Optional and Computed attribute keeps the ID already in state, so the resolver returns without a lookup and that ID is sent.
empty-string-selects-lookup.conditions: Narrowed after verification: previously said an empty string always selects a lookup, but on update an empty value for an Optional and Computed attribute keeps the state value. It relies on Terraform treating an empty configured string on such an attribute as unset, which is not shown in a captured source.

removing-id-retains-value.statement: Removing an explicit enrollment_cert_id from the configuration can leave the value already in state in place rather than clearing it.
removing-id-retains-value.conditions: Follows from the attribute being Optional and Computed with Read filling it from the API. It relies on Terraform's usual handling of an Optional and Computed attribute removed from configuration, which is not shown in a captured source.

refresh-does-not-resolve.statement: A refresh only runs Read, which hydrates state from the API response; the resolver runs only inside create and update, so a group whose state holds an empty certificate ID is repaired when an update runs.
refresh-does-not-resolve.conditions: Follows from the resolver being called only in the create and update functions. The healing needs an update to be planned for the resource; whether a plain refresh-only plan never does so is Terraform behavior, not shown in a source.

import-skips-resolver.statement: The App Connector group importer accepts a numeric ID or a name, resolves the name to an ID, and returns; it does not call the enrollment-certificate resolver.
